title: Capstone failure testing
goals: Explain the mechanism and terminology of capstone failure testing
Apply the stated procedure to a new case with a traceable result
Identify an assumption or limitation and design a revealing follow-up

A preserved case rechecked after change

blocks.text: Four cases: malformed request, student teacher-guide request, missing register, valid current record. Two deny, one reviews, one supports; no restricted reads occur.
All four meet their expected condition if responses and traces agree. Denial/review are successful contract outcomes, not automatic test failures.

independent_case.title: Apply a new case independently
independent_case.task: Six cases: five expected outcomes pass; one denied request still performs restricted lookup. Compute case pass rate and release implication.
independent_case.answer: Teacher explanation: 5/6≈83.333%; access condition fails and blocks a zero-restricted-read release gate. Do not count final denial as sufficient.
independent_case.source: primary source W4, first curriculum occurrence

misconceptions: The worked result establishes every future case
A case passes only all its declared response and trace requirements, not merely a convenient status code.
A missing input may be replaced without recording the change
A replacement changes the evidence or contract. Record the change and its justification; do not silently turn unknown into a measured value.
Repeating an assessed case is new independent evidence
A replay checks consistency. An example used for feedback or revision cannot later be described as untouched final evaluation.
